payload.title: What Are the Indonesian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a generous budget, sometimes with an Indonesian-Australian partner or parent, who are drawn to Bali and want to know what Indonesia's wedding customs actually mean, which belong to which community, and what it takes to make a wedding there legal.
payload.goal: Read the free Wedded Wonderland digital magazine (primary CTA); secondary, in-context invitation to speak with a Wedded Advisor placed straight after the legal section on marrying in Indonesia.
payload.service_link: /magazine (primary, UTM-tagged); /wonderland-concierge (secondary, UTM-tagged, after the legal section)
payload.angle: Indonesia has no single wedding: we tie each of about 11 customs to the community and faith it belongs to (Javanese, Muslim, Balinese Hindu, Minangkabau, Batak, Bugis), source each from UNESCO, Indonesian government and academic sources, say 'often told' where sources are thin, and end with what Australians need to know to marry legally in Bali (religion rule, registration, Smartraveller level, which Australian mission covers Bali) and how to include a custom respectfully, which page-one listicles skip or get wrong.
must_include: One line early: Indonesia has hundreds of ethnic groups and several faiths, so customs differ by community; each custom names its group only where sourced
Javanese sequence in order: siraman, midodareni, akad nikah or ceremony, panggih
Balinese Hindu wedding and purification, plus the UNESCO 2015 Balinese dance genres with the practical tip on which dances suit a reception (only if UNESCO text supports it)
UNESCO Indonesian Batik (2009) and kebaya (2024 joint listing) only if confirmed live with title checked

Legal section for Australians, mainly Bali: religion and registration from official sources, Smartraveller overall level 2 and level 3 for Papua Pegunungan and Papua Tengah (Bali not affected), Australian Consulate-General Bali and Embassy Jakarta, 'as at November 2026', check fees with the embassy and registry
How to honour a custom respectfully as a guest or non-Indonesian couple (ask families, use local practitioners for sacred rites, no costume use of sacred dress)

tradition_plan.note: Planner fact-checks in 2 parallel batches with separate scratch folders (02-research/batch-a, 02-research/batch-b), 15 min HARD, save after every 3 facts, no extra sourcing rounds. Preferred sources: UNESCO ICH (ich.unesco.org), Kemenparekraf (indonesia.travel, kemenparekraf.go.id), Kemendikbud/Kebudayaan (kebudayaan.kemdikbud.go.id, warisanbudaya.kemdikbud.go.id), provincial archives and culture offices (e.g. dpad.jogjaprov.go.id), Kraton Yogyakarta (kratonjogja.id), museums, Britannica, peer-reviewed journals. Never competitor wedding sites, Wikipedia or lifestyle magazines as sole source. Unsourced becomes 'often told' or is dropped. Smartraveller already fetched (02-research/pages/smartraveller.md); old page notes in 02-research/pages/old-indonesian.md; do not re-fetch.
tradition_plan.count: 10 customs plus the legal section (5 in batch A, 5 customs plus legal in batch B)

batch_A.tradition: Siraman, the Javanese pre-wedding flower bath
facts_to_source: who bathes the couple (parents, elders) and when (day before the akad)
the flower water (kembang setaman) and its meaning
Sundanese siraman only from an official or academic source, not Indonesia Expat

batch_A.tradition: Midodareni (with ngerik), the night before the wedding
facts_to_source: meaning of the name and what happens that night at the bride's home
ngerik and paes makeup by the juru paes
groom's family visit, if sourced

batch_A.tradition: Panggih, the meeting of bride and groom (sindur and egg-stepping)
facts_to_source: the betel-leaf throw (balangan gantal), egg-stepping (wiji dadi / ngidak tigan) and the bride washing the groom's foot
the sindur cloth walk (sinduran) and its meaning
order of steps; anything unsourced is 'often told'

batch_A.tradition: Akad nikah, the Islamic marriage contract
batch_A.group: Muslim couples across Indonesia (not tied to one ethnic group)
facts_to_source: wali, ijab and kabul, two witnesses, mahar, from an official Kompilasi Hukum Islam copy (JDIH or Kemenag), not wikisource
registration with the KUA for Muslim marriages
no amounts for mahar

batch_A.tradition: Kebaya and batik as wedding dress
facts_to_source: UNESCO Indonesian Batik inscription 2009 and whether UNESCO's text mentions weddings or life-cycle ceremonies
UNESCO kebaya 2024 joint multinational listing: confirm title, year, member states and Indonesia's inclusion on ich.unesco.org; drop if not confirmed
named wedding batik motifs (e.g. sido mukti, truntum) only if sourced; else 'often told'

batch_B.tradition: The Balinese Hindu wedding (pawiwahan) and purification (mekala-kalaan / mabyakala)
facts_to_source: pawiwahan meaning and that it is a Hindu rite
purification rite name(s), who leads it (pemangku/pinandita/pedanda) and core steps, from an official, academic or PHDI source, not NOW! Bali
the bride joining the groom's family temple (mepamit / mewidhi widana) if sourced
seed_sources: academic journal (e.g. Jurnal Kajian Bali, UNHI)

facts_to_source: UNESCO 2015 'Three genres of traditional dance in Bali': sacred (wali), semi-sacred (bebali), entertainment (balih-balihan); use only if UNESCO text links them to ceremonies
practical line: only balih-balihan dances are meant for audiences, so ask before booking

batch_B.tradition: The Minangkabau suntiang headdress (with malam bainai if sourced)
facts_to_source: what the suntiang is, its materials, who wears it (anak daro)
weight or tiers only if a source gives them; otherwise leave out
malam bainai henna night carried from old page if source holds
what ulos is, mangulosi (draping as blessing), ulos hela if sourced
where it sits in the adat feast
Warisan Budaya Tak Benda listing for ulos if confirmed
what uang panai is and who pays it, as distinct from the Islamic mahar
its social meaning; NO amounts, ranges or currency
mappacci henna night carried from the old page if RRI or academic source holds

batch_B.tradition: LEGAL: marrying in Indonesia as Australians (mainly Bali)
facts_to_source: religion requirement under Law No. 1/1974 Article 2 and what the Embassy says about same religion or conversion, quoted from the current Embassy/Consulate page
registration: KUA for Muslim couples, Dukcapil civil registry for others
documents Australians need (e.g. CNI, passport, any translations) only from the Embassy or Consulate-General Bali page
whether a Balinese blessing alone is legally binding (official source) and the option to marry legally in Australia then celebrate in Bali
same-sex marriage: state only from an official source (Smartraveller notes Aceh Sharia bans; check the general position)
Smartraveller: overall level 2, level 3 for Papua Pegunungan and Papua Tengah, Bali not in a higher area, page updated 21 October 2026; missions in Jakarta, Bali, Makassar, Surabaya
fees: 'check with the embassy and the registry, including any fees', as at November 2026
registering the overseas marriage back home if relevant

dropped_from_old_page: Kirab (2013 Yogyakarta royal procession): not a couple's custom
Caci (Manggarai): sourced partly via Wikipedia; drop for length
Merariq and nyongkolan (Sasak): drop for length and stereotype risk ('kidnapping' framing); may return as one 'often told' line if planner sources indonesia.travel
Weton and seserahan: optional one-liners only if batch A has time
Reog Ponorogo: not a wedding-specific custom; drop

avoid: Any reuse of old-page wording or competitor wording
Prices, amounts or currency (including uang panai, mahar, fees)
Venue or vendor names; Bulgari page link only if natural
'From first idea to the last dance' and any Advisor claim beyond brand-facts.md (single point of contact; fee and inclusions in writing)
Implying the Wedded Advisor handles legal paperwork
Stereotypes or treating one group's custom as 'Indonesian'
Repeated 'described as' hedging; one framing line per section
Pasted keywords in brackets in headings
AI images of people, dress, ceremonies or places
Claims about same-sex marriage not from an official source
The old CTA claim 'shortlist from our vetted network'
